scenes.say: The tyre looks fine, yet the driver is losing a second a lap. What happened to it?
Graining starts when the tyre slides. The surface tears into little rolls of rubber, and grip drops.
It usually happens on a cold track, or when the tyre is loaded up before it's warm.
Blistering starts inside the tyre when it overheats. Bubbles form and chunks of rubber tear out of the tread.
There's no saving that tyre. A driver can lose a second or more a lap, and the only fix is a pit stop.
Follow every driver's tyre age and pit stops live on LapRadar.

title: Graining vs blistering: what actually happened to that tyre
